_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local trainers for band5_stronghold_approach. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order trainers are placed. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 5000-5999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

trainers.name: Patrolman Verrick
trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Outer Works: patrol trainer'. The first Team Tether body the player meets inside the stronghold's own works, and the lowest rank on Sec36's ladder -- a grunt on a walk, not a gatekeeper. Two creatures, both a little above the captains' band: this fight's job is to tell an under-levelled party to turn around while turning around is still cheap.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: same (-141.8,+7775.4) offset as stronghold.json's `site.at` (141.8,-215.4)->(0,7560), since this fallback mirrors the room's own (translation-only) position.
trainers._position_note: FALLBACK ONLY. scripts/world/stronghold.gd places this row from data/config/stronghold.json's `gauntlet` block, because the coordinates of a spot inside a room belong to the room. This is the same point, written out so the row still stands somewhere sane if the building ever fails to build.
trainers._comment_base_t1_hall_3: T1-HALL-3, 2026-08-30. REVERTED to the rank's shared oxblood grunt silhouette. JUDGE-5 (D2, ranked 2nd of 16) read the officer_b body in H-07-courtyard blind and called it "from a different game": cel-shaded anime, flat blown-out white face, painted eye and mouth, hair as a solid magenta mass, in a world of painted stylised realism -- and said the swap away from hall0830's oxblood grunt "cost style cohesion and cost the Team Tether colour identity". That is a property of the generated atlas, not of the override mechanism: the three Meshy cast bodies used inside the Hall (grunt_c/officer_b/captain_a) all carry the same anime idiom and a purple-magenta palette with no oxblood in it (measured: mean lit RGB (76,57,60) for officer_b against the grunt rig's (73,52,52) maroon). The rank system's own default base IS `grunt` for all three ranks, so deleting the override restores the body the judge preferred with no other change; rank stays legible through the badge/palette layer exactly as before. T3-INSTALL's per-individual identity goal is sound and is not reopened for NPCs outside the Hall -- this reverts only the three bodies standing in the frames JUDGE-5 condemned.

trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Courtyard / Hall Approach: trainer fight'. An officer on Sec36's ladder, and the first three-creature team in the building -- the step up from the patrol is a whole extra creature, not just levels, because that is what actually punishes a party of two.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same offset as stronghold_patrol above.

trainers.name: Keeper Hald
trainers._comment: SG38, spec Sec8 'Tether Chamber Approach: elite trainer'. Captain rank, three creatures of three different types, and the hardest fight before the Warden. His defeat flag is also the ONE door in the complex: data/config/stronghold.json's tether_approach->warden_arena passage is `gated_by_flag: defeated_stronghold_elite`, so he is not a fight the player can walk around. The recovery point sits behind him, which is the order Sec8 asks for -- elite, then rest, then the Warden.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same offset as stronghold_patrol above.

trainers.name: Warden Aldis
trainers._comment: R8.3, spec Act VI step 35 and M14 -- the chapter's last fight. THERE IS NO BOSS MODE AND NO BOSS SCRIPT. He is an ordinary row of this same table: the same team schema, the same reward schema, the same defeat flag, the same encounter_director.begin_trainer_battle(), the same sequential send-out, and catching refused exactly as it is refused for every other trainer in the game (a trainer's creatures are theirs -- CLAUDE.md's hard rule). What makes him the boss is the ONLY thing spec sec12 says makes a boss: a full team of five and the highest levels in the chapter.
trainers._comment_character: Spec sec33 gives him a worldview rather than a motive, and the lines are in data/dialogue/stronghold.json. He is not a moustache-twirler: he believes separation prevents chaos and that ordinary people do not understand the risks, he confirms the readout rather than denying it, and he does not recant when he loses. His face is still PAINTED rather than modelled (HANDOFF sec6) -- flagged, not faked. Sec20 covers creatures, so a Warden face sheet is legal under sec22's budget, but it is owner-gated art and no generation was spent here.
trainers._comment_rank: data/config/npc_ranks.json's top tier -- the crimson badge at its largest, on the Warden's own rig. He is the rig every other Team Tether rank in the chapter has been a variant of, met last and unmodified.
trainers._comment_ow5d: OW5D relocation, same (-141.8,+7775.4) offset as stronghold.json's `site.at`, since this fallback mirrors the room's own (translation-only) position.
trainers._position_note: FALLBACK ONLY, and it mirrors the Warden Arena's own centre-ish point. scripts/world/stronghold_climax.gd places him from the `warden_stand` mark that R8.2's data/config/stronghold.json registers, because a room's coordinates belong to the room. Written out so the row still stands somewhere sane if the building ever fails to build.
trainers._comment_team: A FULL team of five -- the only trainer in the chapter who fields one, and the first time the player's own five-creature limit is met by an equal. Levels 16-20 sit above SF34's captains (10-16) with the ace a clear step above the rest. Three types across the five so no single answer sweeps it: two Ground, one Water, one Air, and a Ground ace. ALL TUNABLE.
trainers._comment_defeat_flag: R8.4 waits on exactly this id: data/config/stronghold_climax.json gates the tether machine shut until it is set, so a player who sprints past him cannot reach the Legendary Chamber's lever with the boss still standing. Spec sec28's order is not optional and this flag is where that is enforced. SG44's world event reads `legendary_freed`, not this.

trainers.name: Watchman Corr
trainers._comment: BAND5-CONTENT. Prompt 66: 'ordinary faction patrols/checkpoints to build pressure before the interior... do not consume every major combat beat before the stronghold.' Every named Team Tether fight in this band used to stand in the same 12m span at the Hall's own doorstep (z 7557-7569) -- four fights stacked at the door and 560m of open, unoccupied ground in front of them. This is the FIRST body the player meets after the three-Sigil approach opens: a lone grunt on a walk, floor-of-band level, at the mouth of the region rather than its threshold. His job is the same one `quarry_picket_dorn` had at the start of Band 2 -- tell an unready party this ground is not free, cheaply, before the real cost arrives.
trainers._why_here: 12m off the spine's own first band-5 waypoint (-80,7120), on the meadow side of the mouth burrowback cluster (order 5000, centre (-85,7125) r18) rather than inside it -- close enough that the two reinforce the same read (drained ground, something dug in, something posted) without a wild aggro chase landing on top of a challenge prompt. Facing back down the road toward where the player enters the band, by eye, the same way `south_bridge_grunt`/`quarry_picket_dorn`'s own facing values are tuned rather than computed.
trainers._why_team: The same two species this exact stretch of ground already fields wild (spawns.json orders 5000/5002) -- his own creatures came off this land, not out of a barracks. Floor of the band's [15,20] trainer range: this fight is a doorbell, not an obstacle.
trainers._comment_base_0830: T3-INSTALL, 2026-08-30. Assigns this individual a distinct generated body (docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md's T1-NPC-CAST entries) instead of the rank's shared 'grunt' silhouette -- see npc_ranks.gd::config_for()'s base_override. The rank badge/palette still applies on top, so rank stays legible at a glance and identity now differs too.

trainers.name: Warder Ness
trainers._comment: BAND5-CONTENT. The escalation step between `stronghold_outer_watch` and the doorstep gauntlet: an OFFICER (npc_ranks.json's ladder, one rung above grunt, the same rank `stronghold_courtyard`'s Warder Solene holds) standing just past the three-Sigil gate (`playground_world.gd`'s SIGIL_GATE_AT, (0,7400)) rather than before it. The gate itself already tells the player this ground is sealed to the unprepared; this fight tells them what is on the other side of that seal -- occupied, ranked, and getting worse. Three creatures against the outer watch's two, levels a step above his, still inside the band's [15,20] table and still below the courtyard's own 16-17.
trainers._comment_base_t1_cast: T1-CAST, 2026-08-30, owner directive: use the bodies that were generated. `officer_b` is the body JUDGE-5 (D2) condemned in the Warden's courtyard, and T1-HALL-3 answered that correctly for THAT frame -- the chapter's climax room is the last place to run an unresolved art-style risk -- but the answer left the asset standing nowhere, and the game's only two officer fights (Dell here in band 3, Ness here) were both wearing officer_a. This lane fixed the defect where it lived instead: `tools/regrade_tether_textures.py` measured the purple/magenta share of each generated Tether atlas against the hand-built rigs (production rigs 0.0-0.1%, generated cast 19.6-34.8%, officer_b worst at 34.8%) and rotated that band onto the hue the shipped `grunt` rig already sits at, bringing all seven to 0.0-0.4%. With the body in the faction's own colour, it can carry an officer fight. Placed at the Sigil-gate checkpoint rather than back in the courtyard: the courtyard keeps the shared oxblood grunt silhouette JUDGE-5 preferred, this spends the body one room earlier, and the two officers stop being the same person twice.
trainers._why_here: Between spine waypoints (80,7370) and (20,7480), 44.1m past the three-Sigil gate along the player's own line of travel -- the first thing they see once the gate opens is this fight, not open meadow. BAND5-CONTENT correction: this read '25m past the Sigil gate on the bearing the gate's own leaf turns to face', which described a gate the road did not actually pass. This lane's driven run measured the gate at (0,7400) sitting 55.9m off the spine (and 60.2m from Ness), and moved it onto the road at (63.6,7400); the 44.1m above is measured from that site by `tools/_probe_band5_sigil_gate.gd`. His 4.0m prompt and the gate's 4.2m are nowhere near contesting. 55m clear of the duskhush cluster at the gate (order 5002, centre (85,7375) r18) and well outside the trailpup cluster ahead (order 5003, centre (20,7485) r16), so neither wild aggro nor either cluster's own radius contests his 4.0m challenge prompt.
trainers._why_team: Trailpup and galecrest are this band's own wild roster (spawns.json orders 5003/5001); mosshell is `stronghold_courtyard`'s own species, met here a room early and wilder for it, the same continuity the mudsnout special encounter (spawns.json order 5004) uses. Three creatures, one level above the outer watch, and the escalation reads: the further in, the more the checkpoint fields.
trainers._comment_base_superseded: T1-CAST, 2026-08-30. T3-INSTALL's `base: officer_a` was here, DUPLICATING the `base` key this entry now carries near the top -- a JSON object with the same key twice keeps the last one, so the override up there was silently dead until this was removed. Removed rather than moved: the reasoning it carried (give an individual a distinct generated body instead of the rank's shared silhouette, rank stays legible through the badge/palette layer) is unchanged and now lives on the surviving `base` key, which names `officer_b` so that the game's only two officer fights stop being the same body twice.
